title: The Reading Room Blackout

intro.storyOn: The reading room has gone quiet. A folio is missing, a door bell failed, and the committee wants a name before supper. Review the records before writing the account. This is an original experimental case, separate from Wrenmere canon.
intro.storyOff: Use the records to classify claims as supported, contradicted or not established. Supported follows from the records; contradicted conflicts with them; not established has both possible and impossible examples. Choose the smallest sufficient source set. This is an experimental case.

ending.storyOn: Your account fixes the removal window and explains why the silent bell proves so little. It does not name a culprit. Ari and Bea both had access; these records do not decide between them. The missing folio remains the next question, not a licence to accuse.
ending.storyOff: Established: the removal window, the disabled bell and who had access. Not established: which permitted person removed the folio or whether the side door opened. A complete exercise can end with an unresolved attribution.

provenance: Original fictional case authored for the owner-requested Postern research program, 27 September 2026. Not adapted from a historical incident or an existing game. Provisional teaching specimen, not human-calibrated or canonical Wrenmere content.

records.title: Two checks
records.source: Reading-room check sheet, fictional primary record.

text.storyOn: At the instantaneous 18:02 check, the folio was on its stand. At the instantaneous 18:08 check, it was absent. The clocks used for both checks were synchronized.
text.storyOff: At the instantaneous 18:02 check, the folio was on its stand. At the instantaneous 18:08 check, it was absent. The clocks used for both checks were synchronized.

records.title: Scope of this exercise
records.source: Explicit author model, not a witness statement.

text.storyOn: For this small exercise, the folio was removed exactly once, without being returned, at a whole-minute mark strictly between the checks. Treat the supplied observations as accurate. This discrete model is not a claim that real investigations have minute-perfect knowledge.
text.storyOff: For this small exercise, the folio was removed exactly once, without being returned, at a whole-minute mark strictly between the checks. Treat the supplied observations as accurate. This discrete model is not a claim that real investigations have minute-perfect knowledge.

records.title: A silent corridor
records.source: Caretaker hearing log, fictional primary record.

text.storyOn: The caretaker heard no bell between the two checks. This record reports only what was heard, not whether the side door opened.
text.storyOff: The caretaker heard no bell between the two checks. This record reports only what was heard, not whether the side door opened.

records.title: The disconnected bell
records.source: Electrician work slip, fictional primary record.

text.storyOn: The side-door bell was disconnected continuously from 18:03 through 18:07 inclusive. The door could still open. While disconnected, opening or closing it could not sound the bell.
text.storyOff: The side-door bell was disconnected continuously from 18:03 through 18:07 inclusive. The door could still open. While disconnected, opening or closing it could not sound the bell.

records.title: Who could reach the stand
records.source: Complete access roster for this fictional exercise.

text.storyOn: Only Ari and Bea had access to the folio between the checks. Both could reach the stand during the entire interval. Cleo was elsewhere and had no access. Access does not establish that a person took anything.
text.storyOff: Only Ari and Bea had access to the folio between the checks. Both could reach the stand during the entire interval. Cleo was elsewhere and had no access. Access does not establish that a person took anything.

records.title: One removal, two candidates
records.source: Explicit author model, not an accusation.

text.storyOn: The removal was performed by one person with access. There was no automated mechanism, accomplice or additional visitor. The available records contain no observation identifying which candidate performed it.
text.storyOff: The removal was performed by one person with access. There was no automated mechanism, accomplice or additional visitor. The available records contain no observation identifying which candidate performed it.

prompt.storyOn: Classify each claim, then choose its smallest sufficient set of records. Do not select every source simply because it is visible.
prompt.storyOff: Classify each claim, then choose its smallest sufficient set of records. Do not select every source simply because it is visible.

text.storyOn: The bounded-window claim is supported by Checks + Scope. Exact-five is not established: 18:04 and 18:05 are both allowed. Before-two is contradicted by the present folio at 18:02 and the one-removal model. Each claim uses Checks + Scope.

text.storyOn: Bell-silent is supported by the hearing log. Door-unused is not established using the log + work slip: an opening while disconnected would also be silent. Bell-live is contradicted by the work slip, which includes 18:05.
